title: False algebraic generalization
guidance: After verifying a special case or visible pattern, state the corresponding algebraic identity or recurrence as if it held generally without proving the induction or coefficient comparison.

preconditions: proof uses examples, pattern matching, recurrence terms, or polynomial identities

title: Divide by a possibly zero term
guidance: Simplify an equation by cancelling or dividing by an expression whose nonzero status has not been established, while leaving the step locally plausible.

preconditions: proof manipulates equations or factors without tracking exceptional cases

title: Inequality direction slip
guidance: Replace a needed sharp inequality with a nearby but insufficient bound, or reverse the monotonic implication after applying a transformation.

preconditions: proof chains inequalities or optimizes an expression

title: Smuggled coprimality
guidance: Use cancellation, modular inversion, or Chinese remainder reasoning as if two quantities were coprime, without proving the needed gcd condition.

preconditions: proof uses modular arithmetic, divisibility, or cancellation modulo an integer

title: Residue lifting gap
guidance: Prove a congruence modulo a smaller modulus and then treat it as if it established the required stronger modulus or divisibility statement.

preconditions: proof moves between congruences modulo related integers

title: Density-to-infinite gap
guidance: Turn a heuristic abundance, interval-length, or residue-class argument into an infinitude conclusion without proving the required coverage for infinitely many parameters.

preconditions: proof aims to show infinitely many integers or divisibility instances

title: Hidden geometry case
guidance: Use an angle chase or cyclicity claim that is correct in the drawn configuration but silently fails for another orientation, ordering, or degeneracy.

preconditions: proof depends on a diagram, angle chase, or cyclic quadrilateral

title: Similarity order swap
guidance: Assert a similarity or congruence with vertices in a plausible but incorrect correspondence, causing the derived ratio or angle equality to be unsupported.

preconditions: proof uses similar triangles, congruence, or proportional lengths

title: Unproved incidence claim
guidance: Introduce a collinearity, concurrence, tangency, or perpendicularity fact as visually evident, then build a correct-looking argument on that unproved incidence.

preconditions: proof uses incidence or metric facts from a geometric construction

title: Double-counting scope mismatch
guidance: Count two related but nonidentical sets as if they were the same, usually by changing whether boundary cases, ordered pairs, or repeated objects are included.

preconditions: proof counts objects in two ways or partitions into cases

title: Pigeonhole threshold slip
guidance: Apply pigeonhole or averaging with a threshold off by one, replacing a strict inequality or ceiling/floor condition with a nearby insufficient version.

preconditions: proof uses pigeonhole, averaging, or extremal thresholds

title: Weak induction state
guidance: Use an induction hypothesis that is slightly weaker than what the next step requires, then proceed as if it controlled the stronger configuration.

preconditions: proof uses induction on size, graph order, or number of objects

title: Unjustified limit interchange
guidance: Swap a limit, sum, integral, derivative, or supremum with another operation without verifying convergence, continuity, compactness, or domination conditions.

preconditions: proof manipulates limiting processes or infinite expressions

title: Boundary attainment gap
guidance: Claim a maximum, minimum, fixed point, or equality case is attained while omitting the compactness, closedness, or endpoint argument that makes attainment valid.

preconditions: proof optimizes a function or uses extremal values

title: Epsilon dependency slip
guidance: Choose a parameter depending on a variable that should have been fixed uniformly, making an epsilon-delta or uniform convergence argument circular.

preconditions: proof uses epsilon-delta, uniform bounds, or quantified parameter choices
